account: Researchers studied PROMPTS at 40 Kenyan health facilities. The platform combined health information, reminders, and a helpdesk that classified questions for automated replies or clinical review. The trial enrolled 6,139 pregnant women between November and December 2021 and followed them through August 2022. Women at facilities assigned to introduce PROMPTS had improvements of 0.06–0.09 standard deviations across five measures of knowledge, preparation, and reported care. Care-seeking for danger signs did not improve significantly. The trial evaluated the whole platform and was not powered for clinical outcomes. The natural-language processing system changed during this period: the technical paper dates the deployment of TRIM-AI to June 2022. Jacaranda Health reported cumulative reach of 3,580,095 mothers across 23 Kenyan counties and 1,500 facilities during July–September 2025. Talk Africa reported on 13 October 2026 from Bungoma County that a first-time mother found that the messages taught her about nutrition and danger signs. In the same report Victor Barasa, a doctor at Malindi Sub-County Hospital, cautioned against overreliance on automated systems and said that doctors must use their own clinical judgment. Jacaranda Health's head of programs told the reporter that some mothers have no phone or cannot read Kiswahili.

value.role: SHA-256 of the complete public case and its assessments

display.answer: Women received scheduled messages and reminders and could text the helpdesk. Clinicians handled questions that required human review.

value.text: Women received scheduled messages and reminders and could text the helpdesk. Clinicians handled questions that required human review.

purpose: Deliver pregnancy and postpartum information by SMS and triage incoming questions to a clinical helpdesk by intent and priority.

ratings.reason: Women had measurable improvements in knowledge and reported care practices.

echoes.setting: eHealth Africa and Jacaranda Health launched PROMPTS in Kano State, Nigeria, for an initial 25,000 mothers

must_hold: Access to a phone that can receive text messages
produced_by: An NLP helpdesk that sorted questions for replies or clinical review

revisions.change: Record drafted from the cited sources.
Paired with AI Incident Database incident 545 (medium confidence); severity not given by the source.

Reworded the helpdesk description so that roughly 86% of messages receive automated guidance and only escalations reach clinical agents, and restated authorship so that Harvard holds the first and joint senior authorships, the IPA authors did data curation, investigation and supervision, five authors are Jacaranda Health employees, and the USAID DIV and Gates grants were awarded to the Jacaranda Health team.
Benefit type set to Improved Physical Health under Trustible's full taxonomy of 23 types; it was Improved Learning among the six first used.
Added what the benefit is measured against, what happened since from the cited sources.
Country of the developer and the deployer added from the organization's own site or a registry.
Rewrote a rating reason, the account and the statement of the system's part in shorter sentences and expanded the abbreviations, leaving the facts and quotations unchanged.
Updated the system details, methods, outcomes, limitations, costs and source lineage from the original evidence and supporting material.

Removed the link to AI Incident Database incident 545. Drops 545 because PROMPTS uses AI to sort incoming questions for a human clinical helpdesk while Tessa gave automated advice directly; no incident involves AI triage of patient health messages.
Added one source, an independent one; recorded one other attempt to repeat the benefit.
Edited the headline, summary, metric, account of events for accuracy and clarity; restated earlier revision notes.

summary: Women at Kenyan facilities that introduced PROMPTS, a text-message platform whose helpdesk sorts questions automatically, had improvements of 0.06–0.09 standard deviations across five measures.
system: PROMPTS, an SMS health platform with automated message classification and a clinical helpdesk; TRIM-AI was introduced in June 2022
taxonomy_note: The trial measured health knowledge and reported care practices, not clinical outcomes.
title: PROMPTS improves pregnant women’s knowledge and reported care in Kenya
